title: How Many Words Are Subsequences of the Text?

concept.title: Wait for the next letter in a bucket
body: A word is a **subsequence** of the text when its letters appear in the text in the same order (not necessarily next to each other). Testing every word against the text costs `|text|` per word. Instead, scan the text **once** and keep all words that are still in the game in **buckets by the letter they are waiting for**: a word that needs `c` next sits in the bucket of `c`.

When a letter of the text arrives, only the words that wait for exactly this letter are advanced, each by one position. Every word moves at most `len(word)` times in total, so the work is `|text| + total length of all words`, however many words there are. Taking the whole group out before refilling the buckets makes sure that a word advances only **one** step for one letter of the text.

statement: Given a text `s` and `n` words, count how many of the words are subsequences of `s` (their letters occur in `s` in the same order, possibly with other letters in between). Equal words are counted separately.
inputFormat: The first line has the text `s`.
The third line has the `n` words.
outputFormat: Print the number of words that are subsequences of `s`.
constraints: Each word has 1 to 30 lowercase letters.

examples.note: a, acd and ace are subsequences; bb is not.

hints: Scanning the text once is enough if you remember which letter every word waits for.
Keep buckets: for each letter the words (with their position) that wait for it.
When a letter arrives, take its whole bucket, advance each word, and put it into the bucket of its next letter.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

s = input().strip()
n = int(input())
w = input().split()

# Your code here

explanation: Words wait in buckets for their next letter. One pass over the text advances exactly the words that wait for the current letter, and a word that reaches its end is counted.
solution.complexity: Time O(|s| + total length of words), space O(total length).
